en: Now, configuring HTMX is one important thing
you sometimes might need to do. Another
important HTMX feature is that you can add
extensions to extend the HTMX functionality
beyond its default functionality.
And there are some officially supported
extensions, but also some extensions that
are provided by the community.
And the idea behind these extensions really
just is that they
add extra features or functionalities.
For example, here I wanna add the debug
extension to
HTMX and therefore here I'll actually grab
this code of this extension.
As you can tell, this is a pretty
straightforward basic extension, but I'll
grab this code
and in my project in the public folder, I'll
add a new file and I'll name it
HTMX-ext-debug.js.
The file name does not matter, but I wanna
make it clear that this is an extension
and you find that file attached so that you
can also use it.
And then here in the index.js file where I
import all these scripts after importing
HTMX, I will also import this newly added
HTMX-ext-debug.js script.
With that, the extension is loaded but not
yet activated.
To activate it, you have to add a special
attribute to the element that wants to use
this extension.
Now, the idea behind this debug extension is
that it listens to all those HTMX-triggered
events and outputs some debug messages,
and therefore I will actually add it to the
body element as a whole.
And you do
add it and enable it for that element and
all the child elements by using the hx-debug
attribute.
And then by providing the name of the
extension between those quotes.
In this case, the extension is called debug.
So here it's this debug name which I specify
between the quotes.
With that, if I save that, if I reload this
page, I actually don't see anything yet
because my console actually hides those
debug messages and I have to enable that by
clicking here, in the console in my DevTools
on default levels and then on verbose. And I
have to enable that. And now I see all these
messages here that are coming from that
debug extension.
So as you can see, it outputs a lot because
it logs all those events that occur
as HTMX is doing its job.
Therefore, I'll disable this again, but this
is an example for an extension added to your
website.
